counterfactual_rationale: The record says hidden_states were mutated in-place when shared_experts_stream=None, corrupting DeepSeek output on ROCm. Varying execution/stream scheduling or explicitly testing the no-shared-stream path could plausibly have exposed the corruption.

The fix restores causal sliding-window image visibility for DeepSeek V4.1, where image positions could see future or outside-window tokens. Regression tests over image-span boundary positions could plausibly have caught the wrong index/mask semantics.

The guard prevents do_kv_cache_update from running in encoder mode, a circumstance broader than attention forward. A model-level encoder/decoder serving path that updates KV cache could plausibly have exposed the missing guard.

The PR fixes multiple DeepEP+DeepGEMM failures: profile-run OOM from dummy routing, DeepEP workspace assertion, and an FP8 block-quant illegal access from integer overflow. The evidence points to large DP/EP full-stack serving/profile runs as the most plausible pre-merge detector.

The cache kernel read past the block table because offset was not bounded against block_table_stride, and the fix was verified with compute-sanitizer memcheck. A memcheck run on the boundary unit test could plausibly have caught the OOB access.

The record describes reordering DSA indexer CUDA-graph operations to reduce captured stream count from about 22 to 2, and explicitly says it is a pure scheduling reorder with no numeric change. I do not see evidence of a correctness or severe availability failure.

The issue is post-graph-capture KV sizing that omitted KV-canary workspace, causing memory-tight configurations to OOM. A startup/graph-capture sizing test with large KV pools and canary enabled could plausibly have caught it.

The PR fixes a page-size-128 Mamba radix cache bug that the earlier KL threshold missed. Edge tests over page sizes greater than 64 with tighter cache-hit/logprob checks could plausibly have exposed it.
The branch adds a reproducer for garbage outputs with NemotronH MTP plus chunked prefill, a hybrid full-serving interaction. An E2E hybrid/MTP chunked-prefill test could plausibly have caught it.

The bug forced FP8 KV cache despite an explicit bfloat16 override, which cascaded to draft models without a Blackwell FP8 KV backend. A speculative-serving test on Blackwell with an explicit kv-cache-dtype override could plausibly have exposed it.

The NPU DSA top-k seed buffers used a CUDA-style 2D shape where the Ascend sparse attention path required a 3D TND shape, causing graph-capture startup failures. NPU hardware CI for MTP IndexShare could plausibly have caught the shape mismatch.

The per-layer page-first-to-layer-first KV transfer kernels did not receive the layer id, so only layer 0 cache copied correctly. Tests covering multiple layers in the KV transfer kernel could plausibly have caught the wrong indexing.
The fix moves a cutlass import out of the NPU path to avoid an NPU import error. An NPU import/startup job could plausibly have caught the hardware-backend-specific failure.

The PR explicitly guards several kernel OOB edge cases, including negative out_loc sentinels and SWA page-table bounds. Dynamic memory checking or edge-case tests with these sentinels and bounds could plausibly have caught the invalid accesses.

The custom-op registration path had to handle older PyTorch versions that lacked register_fake. A PyTorch-version compatibility matrix for custom-op imports/tests could plausibly have caught the registration failure.

The FA3 fa_skip_kv_cache path under piecewise CUDA graph violated flash_attn_varlen_func's q-vs-cu_seqlens contract for padded short inputs, producing NaN embeddings. A piecewise-graph embedding E2E test with short padded inputs could plausibly have caught it.

The record attributes DSV3 AWQ accuracy problems to FP16 overflow and adds int4-to-BF16 dequantization. Tests with activation/weight distributions that exceed FP16's safe range could plausibly have exposed the accuracy loss.

The record lists several changes (MoE gate dtype, TBO, fake dispatch) and says a bias should be float32, but it does not show the observed failure, accuracy delta, crash, or test result. I could not confidently determine whether it is a kernel-correctness fix from this record.

The record reports an accuracy drop for DSV3 on the AITer backend with DP enabled and fixes extend attention to use absorb attention rather than MHA. A DP-enabled AITer model-accuracy evaluation could plausibly have caught the wrong attention path.

The TPU Pallas backend could hit VMEM OOM for very long max-model-len because VREG spill consumed too much memory. TPU CI that includes long-context attention/page-size settings could plausibly have exposed the OOM.

The ROCm sleep-mode allocator released HIP runtime memory but not physical VRAM, preventing later use by other applications. A ROCm sleep/wake memory-release test could plausibly have caught the resource leak.

The shared-memory broadcast implementation needed memory barriers for cross-process visibility and to prevent data races. Multi-process inference tests with varied reader/writer timing could plausibly have exposed stale or reordered visibility.

The AMD prefix-prefill kernel overflowed offset arithmetic unless bn was cast to int64, producing negative offsets and GPU segfaults. Large-offset tests on AMD hardware could plausibly have caught the overflow.

The prior RoPE cache expansion used a runtime-dependent max_context_len, causing inconsistent cache sizes before CUDA-graph capture and failing EAGLE verification/GSM8K. An EAGLE long-sequence graph-capture test could plausibly have caught the instability.
The per-token FP8 quantization kernel rejected hidden dimensions not divisible by 16, such as 1368. Shape-edge tests over non-multiple-of-16 hidden sizes could plausibly have caught the failure.

The XPU all_reduce returned all zeros under torch.compile because the in-place operation was optimized away by the compiler. XPU hardware CI with torch.compile and an all-reduce accuracy check could plausibly have caught it.

Kimi-Linear with ROCm AITER RMSNormQuantFusion crashed because the fusion expected num_v_heads on an attention object that lacked it. A ROCm AITER model startup/inference test for Kimi-Linear could plausibly have exposed it.

The FA3 Llama4/Qwen-VL failure involved scheduler metadata shape and num-head handling, with linked crashes on long or multimodal inputs. E2E FA3 serving tests for those model/sequence configurations could plausibly have caught it.

The PR fixes nightly failures in pooling/multimodal tests and a speculative decoding command after an earlier change. The record does not expose the low-level root, but nightly E2E/model tests were the plausible detector.

The record describes a silent performance bug where unpacked strides caused a low-latency GEMM path to fall back to cuBLAS, with tests ensuring packed outputs and no numerical issue. I did not see evidence that this was a correctness, crash, or severe availability failure.
